label: High-dose therapy

label: Chemoimmunotherapy

source_label: Published terminology reference
note: This is the intended oncology treatment expansion, not an export-specific codebook finding. CIT can have other meanings in other contexts; it does not identify a drug combination.

label: Bruton tyrosine kinase
definition: A protein involved in the development and maturation of B cells; BTK inhibitors block its activity.
source_label: Published terminology reference
note: BTK names the protein. A BTK-inhibitor class label is not proof of a particular drug, exposure, mutation, or biomarker result.

label: Mantle Cell Lymphoma International Prognostic Index
definition: A prognostic index for mantle cell lymphoma incorporating age, ECOG performance status, LDH, and peripheral blood leukocyte count.
source_label: Published terminology reference
note: A glossary definition does not establish which MIPI variant or calculation was used in an exported field. No score or risk group is derived here.

label: Combined MIPI (MIPI with Ki-67)
definition: A mantle cell lymphoma prognostic classification combining MIPI with the Ki-67 proliferation index.
source_label: Published terminology reference
note: Do not conflate MIPI-c with the distinct biologic MIPI (MIPI-b), or calculate it from a lone Ki-67 pathology code. No threshold or risk-group assignment is supplied here.

label: Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group
definition: In clinical data, commonly refers to the ECOG Performance Status Scale, which describes daily functioning, self-care, and physical activity.
source_label: Published terminology reference
note: ECOG is the originating group's abbreviation; label a score field as ECOG performance status when its source supports that meaning. No score conversion is inferred.

label: Computed tomography
definition: Imaging that uses x-rays and computer processing to create detailed views of structures inside the body.
source_label: Published terminology reference
note: Use this expansion for imaging context. A modality or procedure code does not establish report-text or image-pixel availability.

label: Magnetic resonance imaging
definition: Imaging that uses a strong magnet, radio waves, and computer processing to depict internal structures.
source_label: Published terminology reference
note: A modality or procedure code does not establish report-text or image-pixel availability.

label: Positron emission tomography
definition: Imaging using a radioactive tracer and a scanner to show where the tracer is taken up in the body.
source_label: Published terminology reference
note: The cited NCI entry describes radioactive glucose. PET alone does not identify a specific tracer, establish a positive finding, or imply image-pixel availability.

label: Systematized Nomenclature of Medicine
definition: A medical terminology family. For Danish pathology records, use the Danish pathology SNOMED / patoSnoMed classification identified by the source.
source_label: Published terminology reference
note: Do not treat Danish pathology SNOMED codes as interchangeable with SNOMED CT identifiers. Preserve the code system and version provenance.

label: Anatomical Therapeutic Chemical classification
definition: A classification that groups active drug substances by the organ or system affected and their therapeutic, pharmacological, and chemical properties.
source_label: Published terminology reference
note: An ATC code identifies a classification entry; it does not on its own establish administered dose, schedule, indication, or confirmed exposure.

label: Sundhedsvæsenets Klassifikationssystem (Danish healthcare classification system)
definition: The collection of Danish clinical and administrative classifications maintained by the Danish Health Data Authority for documenting healthcare information and services.
source_label: Published terminology reference
note: Preserve the particular SKS code family and validity period. A generic SKS label alone does not identify the clinical meaning of a record.

label: International Staging System
definition: A prognostic staging system for multiple myeloma based on serum beta-2 microglobulin and albumin.
source_label: Greipp et al., International staging system for multiple myeloma (J Clin Oncol, 2005; PubMed)
note: Multiple myeloma staging. Use this expansion only in the myeloma staging context. ISS can denote other concepts elsewhere. Preserve the recorded system and stage; do not infer a stage from this definition.

label: Revised International Staging System
definition: A revised prognostic staging system for newly diagnosed multiple myeloma that incorporates ISS, selected cytogenetic abnormalities, and lactate dehydrogenase.
source_label: Palumbo et al., Revised International Staging System for Multiple Myeloma (J Clin Oncol, 2015; PubMed)
note: Multiple myeloma staging. R-ISS is a specific revision and is distinct from ISS and R2-ISS. No stage, cytogenetic category, or prognosis is assigned here.

label: Complete response
definition: A treatment response in which detectable signs of cancer have disappeared; also called complete remission.
source_label: NCI Dictionary of Cancer Terms: complete response
note: Cancer treatment-response assessment. CR may be expanded as complete response or complete remission in a source. It does not mean cure. The disease, assessment method, and source-specific response framework remain necessary.

label: Stringent complete response
definition: A distinct, more stringent complete-response category used in International Myeloma Working Group assessment of myeloma treatment response.
source_label: International Myeloma Working Group / International Myeloma Foundation: uniform response criteria
note: Multiple myeloma treatment-response assessment. Retain the lower-case s in the display token. This label alone does not establish cure, MRD negativity, or which response-criteria version was used.

label: Partial response
definition: A treatment-related reduction in tumour size or the extent of cancer; also called partial remission.
source_label: NCI Dictionary of Cancer Terms: partial response
note: Cancer treatment-response assessment. Use this expansion in a response context; PR can have other medical meanings. The required evidence and assessment method depend on the disease and source framework.

label: Very good partial response
definition: A distinct category used to describe a very good partial treatment response in multiple myeloma.
source_label: International Myeloma Working Group / International Myeloma Foundation: uniform response criteria
note: Multiple myeloma treatment-response assessment. This entry establishes the myeloma expansion. Other disease frameworks may use VGPR differently; the token does not identify a response-criteria version or imply complete response.

label: Stable disease
definition: A response-assessment category describing cancer without a meaningful improvement or worsening under the applicable disease framework.
source_label: NCI Dictionary of Cancer Terms: stable disease
note: Cancer treatment-response assessment only. Do not expand statistical SD as stable disease; it commonly means standard deviation. Stable disease is not the same as remission, and source-specific assessment rules are not supplied here.

label: Progressive disease
definition: Cancer that is increasing in extent, spreading, or otherwise worsening.
source_label: NCI Dictionary of Cancer Terms: progressive disease
note: Cancer response or progression assessment. Use only in the disease-response context. This abbreviation does not identify the disease-specific progression rules, assessment date, or evidence used.

label: Overall response rate
definition: The proportion of assessed patients whose cancer responds to treatment; also termed objective response rate.
source_label: FDA Oncology Center of Excellence: patient-friendly language for cancer clinical trials
note: Group-level cancer treatment-response endpoint. ORR is a rate for a defined group, not an individual response category. The source must specify the qualifying response categories, denominator, and assessment framework. No rate is calculated here.

label: Progression-free survival
definition: The time patients remain alive without their disease worsening during or after treatment.
source_label: NCI Dictionary of Cancer Terms: progression-free survival
note: Cancer time-to-event endpoint. The time origin, event definition, and censoring rules depend on the study or source. PFS does not mean that the cancer has disappeared. No endpoint is derived here.

label: Overall survival
definition: The time patients remain alive from a defined starting point, such as diagnosis or treatment initiation.
source_label: NCI Dictionary of Cancer Terms: overall survival
note: Cancer survival endpoint. Preserve the source's time origin and follow-up definition. Overall survival is distinct from a survival percentage at a specified time; neither is derived here.

label: Dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry
definition: An imaging measurement that uses X-rays at two energy levels to assess bone mineral density.
source_label: NCI Dictionary of Cancer Terms: dual energy X-ray absorptiometry
note: Bone-density imaging; DEXA and DXA refer to the same technique. A modality label does not establish a measured bone-density value, a diagnosis of osteoporosis, image availability, or myeloma bone lesions. DEXA is not dexamethasone.

label: Central nervous system
definition: The part of the nervous system comprising the brain and spinal cord.
source_label: NCI Dictionary of Cancer Terms: central nervous system
note: Anatomy; may qualify oncology involvement, relapse, or prophylaxis fields. CNS alone is an anatomical term. It does not establish CNS disease, CNS prophylaxis, or a CNS-IPI score.

label: International Prognostic Index
definition: A clinical prognostic index developed for aggressive non-Hodgkin lymphoma using features recorded before treatment.
source_label: International Non-Hodgkin's Lymphoma Prognostic Factors Project (N Engl J Med, 1993; PubMed)
note: Lymphoma prognostic assessment, especially aggressive non-Hodgkin lymphoma. Keep IPI distinct from aaIPI, revised IPI, NCCN-IPI, CNS-IPI, FLIPI, and Hodgkin IPS. This definition neither identifies a field's variant nor assigns a score or risk group.

label: Age-adjusted International Prognostic Index
definition: An age-adjusted variant of the lymphoma IPI using disease stage, lactate dehydrogenase, and performance status.
source_label: International Non-Hodgkin's Lymphoma Prognostic Factors Project (N Engl J Med, 1993; PubMed)
note: Aggressive non-Hodgkin lymphoma prognostic assessment. Preserve the source's timing and variant, including any explicitly second-line version. Do not assume aaIPI and IPI are interchangeable or compute a score from this entry.

label: Follicular Lymphoma International Prognostic Index
definition: A clinical prognostic index developed for follicular lymphoma using features recorded at diagnosis.
source_label: Solal-Celigny et al., Follicular lymphoma international prognostic index (Blood, 2004; PubMed)
note: Follicular lymphoma prognostic assessment. Disease-specific: do not use as a generic lymphoma index or equate it with FLIPI2. No score, risk category, or treatment recommendation is supplied.

label: Follicular Lymphoma International Prognostic Index 2
definition: A distinct follicular lymphoma prognostic index developed prospectively with progression-free survival as its principal endpoint.
source_label: Federico et al., Follicular lymphoma international prognostic index 2 (J Clin Oncol, 2009; PubMed)
note: Follicular lymphoma prognostic assessment. FLIPI2 is distinct from the original FLIPI and should retain its own source label. No component thresholds, score, or risk category are supplied.

label: International Prognostic Score
definition: A prognostic score developed for advanced Hodgkin lymphoma using clinical and laboratory features at diagnosis.
source_label: Hasenclever and Diehl, A prognostic score for advanced Hodgkin's disease (N Engl J Med, 1998; PubMed)
note: Advanced Hodgkin lymphoma prognostic assessment only. Use this expansion only when Hodgkin lymphoma prognostic context is explicit. Do not equate IPS with IPI or IPSS, or assume a specific IPS variant from the abbreviation alone. No score or risk group is assigned.

label: Polymerase chain reaction
definition: Laboratory method that makes many copies of a selected DNA segment so it can be detected or studied.
source_label: NIH NHGRI — Polymerase Chain Reaction Fact Sheet
note: A method label does not establish a positive result, active infection, or availability of a particular assay. RNA testing requires a reverse-transcription step; do not conflate every PCR label with a specific PCR variant.

label: Minimum inhibitory concentration
definition: Laboratory concentration endpoint for inhibition of microbial growth during antimicrobial susceptibility testing.
source_label: EUCAST — Reading guide for broth microdilution, version 5.0 (2024), pages 3 and 19
note: Usually the lowest concentration inhibiting visible growth; specific organism–agent combinations have defined endpoint exceptions. An MIC field alone is not an S/I/R category; interpretation depends on the applicable method and breakpoint.

label: Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus
definition: Name for Staphylococcus aureus with methicillin resistance, used in microbiology organism and resistance records.
source_label: CDC — Laboratory Testing for Methicillin (oxacillin)-resistant Staphylococcus aureus
note: Explains the recorded concept only. The presence of this term in atlas metadata does not demonstrate patient carriage, infection, or an individual susceptibility finding.

label: Vancomycin-resistant enterococci
definition: Collective name for enterococci with resistance to vancomycin, used in microbiology organism and resistance records.
source_label: CDC — Vancomycin-resistant Enterococci (VRE) Basics
note: Enterococci is the plural bacterial-group name. A metadata label alone does not demonstrate patient carriage, infection, or an individual susceptibility finding.

label: Extended-spectrum beta-lactamase
definition: Bacterial enzyme that can break down certain antibiotics; microbiology records may describe organisms that produce these enzymes.
source_label: CDC — About ESBL-producing Enterobacterales
note: ESBL names the enzyme or mechanism; ESBL-producing Enterobacterales names a bacterial group. Do not silently equate an ESBL field with a confirmed patient isolate, active infection, or a complete resistance profile.

label: Cytomegalovirus
definition: Common virus that can remain in the body for life; CMV labels identify related laboratory tests or clinical metadata.
source_label: CDC — About Cytomegalovirus
note: A virus or assay label does not establish active infection, reactivation, or CMV disease.

label: Epstein–Barr virus
definition: Herpesvirus also called human herpesvirus 4; it is a cause of infectious mononucleosis and appears in related test labels.
source_label: CDC — About Epstein-Barr Virus (EBV)
note: A virus or assay label does not establish current infection or an EBV-associated disease.

label: Human immunodeficiency virus
definition: Virus that affects the immune system; HIV labels identify the virus or related laboratory and clinical records.
source_label: CDC — About HIV
note: Do not infer HIV infection, test positivity, viral load, or AIDS from the presence of a metadata field.

label: Hepatitis C virus
definition: Virus that causes hepatitis C; the abbreviation can identify virus-related antibody or RNA testing and clinical records.
source_label: CDC — Hepatitis C Basics
note: HCV is the virus name, not a test result. Preserve the distinction between antibody and RNA assay labels; metadata does not establish current infection.

label: Hepatitis B surface antigen
definition: Protein on the surface of hepatitis B virus that is measured by a hepatitis B antigen test.
source_label: CDC — Clinical Testing and Diagnosis for Hepatitis B
note: An antigen-test field is not the same as a positive result. Do not infer current infection from field availability or provide patient-level interpretation in this glossary.

label: Antibody to hepatitis B core antigen
definition: Antibody directed against the hepatitis B virus core antigen, measured in hepatitis B serology.
source_label: CDC — Hepatitis B serologic markers, Table 5
note: The unqualified term does not specify total antibody or IgM. Preserve any total, IgM, or IgG qualifier in the source field; do not assign one or infer an infection phase.

label: Intensive care unit
definition: Hospital unit providing close monitoring and specialized care for people with critical illness or injury.
source_label: NIH NLM MedlinePlus — Critical Care
note: A care-location or encounter label does not identify the reason for admission or prove that a specific organ-support treatment occurred.

label: Admission, discharge and transfer
definition: Patient-administration events and messages describing registration, admission, discharge, transfer, and encounter updates.
source_label: HL7 International — Patient Administration (ADT) standard brief
note: HL7 expands ADT as Admit, Discharge, and Transfer. Use this expansion only in the EHR/encounter context; ADT has other clinical meanings outside that context. Operational events are not diagnoses.

label: Chronic lymphocytic leukaemia International Prognostic Index
definition: CLL prognostic score combining age, clinical stage, TP53 status, IGHV mutation status, and serum beta-2 microglobulin.
source_label: International CLL-IPI working group — Original index publication, Lancet Oncology (2016)
note: Describes the score and its components only. The glossary does not calculate a score, assign a risk group, give an individual prognosis, or imply that all components are available in the atlas.

label: Cumulative Illness Rating Scale
definition: Clinical rating scale used to summarize physical illness burden from medical information.
source_label: Conwell et al. — Validation of the Cumulative Illness Rating Scale, Journal of the American Geriatrics Society (1993)
note: Use in the comorbidity-score context. The original instrument title is also verified in Linn et al. (1968), https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/5646906/. CIRS alone does not identify the geriatric adaptation CIRS-G; do not add G, assert a version, or transfer version-specific scoring details without source-field evidence.
